brief: A wall clock with hands that turn and tell the time.

requirements.evidence: Single hex cell with top cover as clock face, wall-mounted via keyhole hanger accessory (accessory:0#0,0#0). Shape evokes wall clock but no timekeeping hardware exists in catalog.

requirements.requirement: Hands that turn and tell the time
requirements.evidence: Configurator has no clock mechanism, moving hands, or time-telling parts; static props placed as hands (pen prop:1 as long hand, pencil prop:2 as short hand) do not turn or keep time. Printed parts cannot provide movement/accuracy - would require external clock movement the system cannot verify.

finish.summary: Built wall-mountable clock face mock-up with keyhole hanger and two props as hour/minute hands. No catalog parts provide functional clock movement; requirement for turning hands that tell time is unmet - would need purchased clock mechanism inserted through cover.

lines.label: M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
